title: Fat Modules, Thin Wrappers: Structuring Code You Can Actually Test — Check

questions.prompt: In Agronomy Studio's structure, where does the soil-classification business logic live?
questions.explanation: Domain logic lives in `netlify/lib/*` modules so it can be tested without HTTP plumbing; the functions are thin wrappers.

questions.prompt: Passing a `source` argument into `classifySoil` lets a test substitute a fake data source instead of hitting the network.
questions.explanation: That is dependency injection: the wrapper supplies the live source while tests supply a fake, avoiding network calls and mocking globals.

questions.prompt: Why are the function wrappers kept deliberately 'dull'?
questions.explanation: Thin wrappers push the interesting, testable logic into modules; the wrappers just parse and serialize, so few tests target them.
options: So they run faster than the modules
Because Netlify forbids logic in functions
So that little worth testing lives in transport code, concentrating tests on the domain modules
To reduce the bundle size of the frontend
